title.narrative: The Gambia Advancing Reforms for Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth (ARISE) DPF1

description.narrative: The development objectives of the First Advancing Reforms for Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth (ARISE) Development Policy Financing Project for Gambia are the following: to lay the foundations for stable growth and better jobs through: (i) enhancing domestic revenue mobilization, (ii) laying key infrastructure, regulatory and skill foundations for private sector development, and (iii) strengthening climate resilience. The operation is the first in a programmatic series of two and financed with an International Development Association (IDA). The reform program is based on three pillars: Pillar 1 - Enhance domestic revenue mobilization. Reforms will broaden the tax base, rationalize tax expenditures, and modernize tax administration. Pillar 2 - Lay key infrastructure, regulatory and skill foundations for private sector development. Reforms aim to foster private sector-led growth by digitalizing business licensing, improving competition and investment climate in selected sectors, while advancing human capital development, with a focus on expanding opportunities for women and youth. Pillar 3 - Strengthen climate resilience. Reforms aim at establishing a legal and institutional framework for climate governance and climate resilience, ensuring that territorial and sectoral planning integrate climate adaptation and disaster risk management.

Result Indicator #6. Price of entry-level broadband services: Data-only mobile-broadband basket, 2GB (% of monthly GNI per capita)

comment.narrative: The Gambia continues to make steady progress in improving broadband affordability. While the ITU revised its global methodology in 2025—shifting from a 2GB to a 5GB minimum data basket—the new 2025 data (8.68% of GNI per capita for 5GB) is normalized to a 2GB equivalent to preserve historical comparability. This normalized value of 3.47% represents a clear improvement from the 2024 baseline of 4.25%, keeping the indicator firmly on track to achieve the 2.00% target by December 2027
